national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu said that today national security extends beyond military capabilities and it requires close cooperation between scientific institutions and the armed forces to translate innovation into practical solutions. She said this during interaction with the faculty and course members of the 66th National Defence College Course at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the security and technological landscapes are changing rapidly, bringing new and complex challenges. President Murmu noted that these developments call for greater preparedness, strategic foresight and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances. She added that the fast decision-making mechanism is also becoming more important because the techniques of modern warfare have expanded into cyber security, space technology, and biotechnology apart from the traditional domains. Further, President Murmu said that recent conflicts have highlighted the importance of cost-effective technologies that complement advanced defence systems and make the best use of available resources. She also underlined the importance of government initiatives such as the Research, Development and Innovation Scheme, for strengthening the link between innovation and national security. The President said that the use of Artificial Intelligence in various domains of science, national security and economic activities is increasing. She said that decision making cannot be outsourced exclusively to this technology and emphasised the need for a balanced approach. The President also underlined that economic resilience is an integral part of the national security framework. She said that the Indian economy has demonstrated its capabilities to absorb disruptions created by external factors. The President highlighted that India has accomplished this without compromising the strategic freedom of action.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 165 PM Modi says digital power has opened up greater opportunities for India; Addresses Bloomberg New...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Centre has embodied the principle of Power to Empower in its governance approach and work culture. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Mr Modi said that India’s progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities. He said that power is not just the ability to move ahead, but it is also the ability to empower others. He said that in the present era, digital power has emerged as one of the key drivers of this transformation and is playing a significant role in advancing this vision. Mr Modi stated that digital power has opened up greater opportunities for India. Prime Minister Modi said that India’s economic growth is taking place on a strong foundation amidst global uncertainty. He said the GDP growth stood at 7.8% in the first quarter of this financial year. Mr Modi highlighted that today, India’s foreign exchange reserves exceed 700 billion dollars and the banking system is in its strongest position in many decades. Prime Minister said India’s reform express continues to move ahead at high speed. Prime Minister said that India’s progress in the twenty-first century is a story of advancing together with everyone and carrying everyone along. He said, whenever the world needs a steady pillar, India extends its hand in support, recognizing its responsibility. Mr Modi said today, India is home to more than two thousand Global Capability Centres that are providing services to companies across the world. Prime Minister said technology, data, knowledge and innovation have become important sources of power in the twenty-first century. He said, the government constant endeavour is to ensure that India’s capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well. Mr Modi said, India is the Mother of Democracy, and it has over 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels.’ Mr Modi highlighted that India had lifted twenty-five crore people out of poverty over the past decade. Prime Minister Modi said India’s startup ecosystem has expanded significantly since 2014, with the number of startups crossing 2,50,000. He noted that nearly half of these startups come from smaller cities and towns, while more than 45% have at least one woman director or partner.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 282 HM Amit Shah hails BIMSTEC as important platform for regional integration, economic cooperation a...
national_raw_news.content: India is hosting the first Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi. This historic meeting highlights the collective commitment to combating terrorism, transnational organized crime, narcotics, radicalization, human trafficking, illicit financial flows, and cyber threats. Speaking on the occasion, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that BIMSTEC has emerged as an important platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. He said India has always been committed to peace and human welfare, guided by the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. Mr Shah reiterated that India respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries and believes in the peaceful resolution of disputes. Reaffirming India’s policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, the Union Home Minister called for a collective commitment to ensure that no terrorist network finds space within the region for shelter, recruitment, training, financing or activities against neighbouring countries. Mr Shah also emphasised mutual assistance in extradition and legal cooperation, in accordance with national laws and applicable treaties. He said criminal networks operate across borders and exploit local vulnerabilities. Mr Shah stressed the need for real-time cooperation and coordination among intelligence, law enforcement, financial monitoring and border management agencies. On counter-terrorism cooperation, the Minister stressed the exchange of actionable intelligence through designated nodal agencies and better coordination against terrorist financing and organised crime. Mr Shah said India has achieved significant success in bringing fugitive criminals back from different parts of the world to face justice. He appealed to all BIMSTEC members to strengthen cooperation to ensure that no criminal or terrorist can evade the law, regardless of where they are hiding. BIMSTEC is a regional organisation established in 1997 to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries around the Bay of Bengal and its neighbourhood. It has seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. It aims to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal and in its neighbourhood.

national_raw_news.title: Shefali Verma, Shubman Gill named ICC Women’s and Men’s Player of Month for September 2026 3 hours ago 85
national_raw_news.content: Indian opener Shafali Verma was named the ‘ICC Women’s Player of the Month’ winner for September 2026, following incredible title-winning outings in the Women’s Asia Cup and the Asian Games with the bat and clutch contributions in high-stakes matches. On the other hand, Indian captain Shubman Gill was named ICC men’s Player of the Month for a record fifth time following his outstanding performance in the One Day International series against the West Indies. It is the second time Shafali has won the monthly award, with the 22-year-old first tasting success in November last year when she helped India claim the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup on home soil, as per the ICC. Shafali Verma, was the highest run-scorer for her team as India won the Women’s Asia Cup. Shubman Gill, as per the ICC, won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza. Gill scored 333 runs in India’s first two One Day Internationals against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets. This is Gill’s fifth ICC Men’s Player of the Month award, after wins in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025, extending his record as the men’s player with the most wins.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Coast Guard inducts indigenous ALH MK-III Helicopter in Maharashtra 3 hours ago 53
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Coast Guard inducted indigenous Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH MK-III) aircraft, CG 875, into the Coast Guard Region (West) at Ratnagiri in Maharashtra today. The aircraft was received at Coast Guard Air Station, Ratnagiri, with a traditional ‘water cannon salute’. The Commanding Officer, ICGAS Ratnagiri, welcomed the aircraft and crew. The induction of ALH MK-III at Ratnagiri marks a significant enhancement in the operational capability of the Indian Coast Guard along the West Coast. The state-of-the-art helicopter is equipped with Advanced Radar, integrated with long-range imaging and identification capabilities through its Electro Optical Pod and Automatic Identification System. The aircraft is additionally equipped for target neutralisation with its cabin mounted 12.7 mm Heavy Machine Gun. These enhanced surveillance, detection, identification and response capabilities will significantly augment the ICG ability to safeguard nation’s maritime interests within the EEZ, especially along the sensitive coast of Maharashtra The induction of CG 875 is particularly significant as it is the first of the allotted five ALH MK-III aircraft to be positioned with 831 Sqn (CG) at Ratnagiri. The progressive induction of the remaining aircraft will substantially augment the Squadron’s operational capability and enable sustained aerial surveillance and response over the vast maritime area of Coast Guard Region (West), which faces diverse challenges owing to its strategic importance and geographical location.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, CM Rekha Gupta launch 5 EV charging stations, inaugurate 13 Air Quality Monitoring Stations 3 hours ago 78
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Environment and Forests Bhupender Yadav, along with Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, launched five public EV charging stations and inaugurated 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations in New Delhi today. Talking to the media, Mr Yadav praised Ms Gupta’s leadership in implementing measures to address air pollution in Delhi, saying that the government had taken steps to put 11 action points into practice at a major pollution hotspot. Highlighting the reported improvement in air quality at the hotspot, Mr Yadav said the Air Quality Index (AQI), which stood at 430 on 30th August, had declined to 92 today. He said that the Delhi government increased the combined fleet of electric and CNG buses to over five thousand 500 in line with the commitment earlier made to the CAQM. The Union Minister added that the government had established charging infrastructure and coordinated the efforts of the Delhi Traffic Police, Public Works Department and other agencies to address pollution. Speaking on the occasion, the Delhi Chief Minister said that the Delhi government is strengthening its fight against pollution through real-time monitoring of air quality. She said that this initiative marks a significant step towards real-time monitoring of the Air Quality Index from every corner of the national capital.

national_raw_news.title: IMD launches interactive cyclone warning system to strengthen disaster preparedness - Odisha TV
national_raw_news.content: IMD launches interactive cyclone warning system to strengthen disaster preparedness Advertisment Weather News IMD launches interactive cyclone warning system to strengthen disaster preparedness IMD launches an interactive cyclone warning system to provide location-specific weather alerts, improve early warnings and strengthen disaster preparedness across India. 13 Oct 2026 14:42 IST Odisha TV Bureau Follow Us IMD launches interactive cyclone warning system Photograph: (PIB) Advertisment The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on October 12, 2026, launched an interactive web-based Decision Support System (DSS) for cyclone warnings and marine weather services, aiming to strengthen disaster preparedness and improve public access to critical weather information. Advertisment The platform was unveiled during IMD’s bi-annual Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting for the post-monsoon season (October–December 2026), chaired by Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of Meteorology, IMD, and Third Vice-President of the World Meteorological Organization. The public can access the platform through the IMD website and the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) website. Advertisment Also Read: Durga Puja fervour to remain high as dry weather likely in Odisha New Platform Offers Location-Specific Cyclone Information The user-friendly, interactive DSS brings cyclone and marine weather information together on a single platform. It is designed to help disaster management authorities, government agencies and the public understand potential hazards and take timely action. Advertisment Through interactive maps and visualisations, users can access information on observed and forecast cyclone tracks, intensity, wind patterns, rainfall, storm surge and rainfall forecasts for river catchments. The system also provides uncertainty cones for cyclone tracks and district-wise rainfall warnings. The platform aims to bridge the gap between weather forecasts and their practical application, enabling better preparedness, informed decision-making and improved public safety during cyclones and other severe weather events. October 12 Holds Significance for India's Cyclone Preparedness The launch coincided with an important milestone in India's cyclone forecasting history. IMD successfully predicted Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Phailin in 2013 and Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Hudhud in 2014. Both cyclones crossed the Indian coast on October 12 in their respective years. These forecasting achievements marked significant progress in the country's disaster preparedness and earned international recognition for India's early-warning capabilities. Over 230 Participants Attend Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting IMD has conducted the bi-annual Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting since 2008 to review preparedness for the upcoming cyclone season, assess progress on previous recommendations and address operational challenges. This year's meeting brought together approximately 230 participants from more than 30 organisations, with around 180 attending online and 50 participating in person. Representatives from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ministry of Home Affairs, Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, Indian Coast Guard and Central Water Commission attended the meeting. State disaster management authorities, fisheries departments and scientific institutions, including the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting and the Indian Institutes of Technology, also participated. Officials and representatives from coastal states and Union Territories, along with various ministries and sectoral agencies, discussed operational requirements and ways to strengthen coordination ahead of the cyclone season. Indian Navy Commissions Indigenous Mahe-Class Anti-Submarine Warfare Craft INS Mangrol in Mumbai Dockyard Thread starter Thread starter PIB Start date Start date Today at 11:35 AM The Indian Navy commissioned INS Mangrol (P82), the third Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), at the Naval Dockyard, Mumbai, on 12 Oct 2026. The commissioning ceremony was presided over by VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. The commissioning ceremony was attended by senior officers of the Defence Forces, representatives of the Ministry of Defence, Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), industry partners and other distinguished dignitaries. Indigenously designed and constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi, INS Mangrol represents India's growing capabilities in warship design, construction and systems integration. With over 80 percent indigenous content, the ship reflects the nation's commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, while highlighting the contribution of Indian defence industries and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) towards strengthening indigenous naval capabilities. Designed for operations in coastal and shallow waters, INS Mangrol is equipped to undertake Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), underwater surveillance and Low-Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), along with mine warfare-related tasks. Its advanced sensors, sonar and weapon systems enhance its capability to detect, track and counter underwater threats in the challenging littoral environment. Powered by three diesel engine-driven waterjet propulsion units, the ship offers high manoeuvrability and rapid response, essential for operations in shallow and confined waters. VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, in his address, congratulated the Indian Navy and CSL on the commissioning of INS Mangrol. He highlighted the importance of indigenous warships in strengthening India's maritime surveillance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in the evolving maritime security environment. He also emphasised the growing capabilities of India's indigenous shipbuilding industry and the Indian Navy's continued commitment to technological advancement, operational preparedness and self-reliance in defence manufacturing. INS Mangrol derives its name from the coastal town and prominent fishing harbour of Mangrol in Junagadh district of Gujarat. The ship also carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until April 2004, continuing the naval tradition of preserving the names of distinguished warships. The commissioning of INS Mangrol marks another significant milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities and coastal defence preparedness. The ship will contribute to safeguarding India's coastal approaches and maritime interests, enhancing maritime domain awareness and countering underwater threats. Its induction further reinforces the Indian Navy's commitment to maritime security, regional stability and self-reliance in warship construction, in furtherance of India's maritime interests in the Indian Ocean Region. To use standard view, enable JavaScript by changing your browser options. होम सभी विशेषताएं विशेषताएं विवरण Economy Khadi & Village Industries: From Tradition to Enterprise Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 11:25AM A charkha spinning in a village once spoke of nationalism. Today, that spirit is taking new shape through a growing ecosystem of rural enterprises. Honey, herbal products, banana fibre, textiles and other village industries are creating new possibilities for traditional skills. The spirit of self-reliance continues to resonate with the vision of Vocal for Local and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Traditional skills and local resources are finding new markets through access to finance, technology and training. This growing connection between local enterprise and consumers is also reflected in the Khadi Mahotsav. The Khadi Mahotsav takes place annually from 2 October to 31 October . With a particular focus on youth, the campaign sensitises them towards Khadi and “Vocal for Local” and encourages the public to buy Khadi and local products. At the centre of this transformation is the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) . It is a statutory body established under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956. The Act mandates KVIC to plan, promote, facilitate, organise and assist village industries. It covers measures related to training, raw materials, marketing, research, and quality improvement . It also supports skill development and research, while providing technical information and facilities related to Khadi and village industries. In 2025–26, sales of Khadi and Village Industries products reached a historic ₹1.87lakh crore, the highest level recorded (as of May 2026). Compared with 2013–14, sales grew by 501%, while production increased by 380% to ₹1,25,296 crore. Employment in the sector increased by 56% to 2.04 crore. The remuneration paid to artisans has also increased. It rose from ₹4 per hank in 2013–14 to ₹15 per hank currently, an increase of approximately 275%. One hank is equivalent to 840 yards of yarn in length and one pound by weight. Building Rural Businesses, One Artisan at a Time From acquiring skills to accessing markets, a range of interventions is supporting artisans and village industries. KVIC has a network of 35 departmental and non-departmental training centres . Training covers food products, bakery, beekeeping, agarbatti, candles, motor repairing and several other activities. During FY 2025-26, 79,682 trainees received training under various KVIC training programs. Women constitute more than 80% of approximately five lakh artisans in the Khadi sector. In 2025–26, 47,382 women received training under various KVIC programmes, accounting for approximately 59% of all trainees. Training is complemented by interventions including toolkit and equipment distribution, marketing support and other measures. Since March 2008, the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) has provided employment opportunities to nearly 97.95 lakh people through KVIC. Daily Excelsior 04:19 AM Oct 13, 2026 IST MP Gulam Ali Khatana along with Director PIB, Neha Jalali inaugurating Multimedia Exhibition at Katra on Monday. Excelsior Correspondent KATRA, Oct 12: Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Gulam Ali Khatana inaugurated an eight-day multimedia exhibition organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), J&K, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, at the Government Higher Secondary School premises in Katra in the presence of Director of CBC and PIB Jammu, Neha Jalali, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (Katra), Piyush Dhotra, and other officials. The outreach drive, themed "12 Saal-Vishwas Ke, Vikas Ke, Jan Kalyan Ke", coincides with the ongoing Navratra festival at Katra that witnesses lakhs of devotees every year to pay obeisance at the revered shrine. Advertisement The inaugural ceremony also focused on themes like Reform Utsav and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Speaking on the occasion, Gulam Ali Khatana highlighted the significant reforms and transformative initiatives undertaken by the Narendra Modi-led Government over the past 12 years, aimed at strengthening the Indian economy, promoting inclusive development and improving the quality of life of citizens. He said that the Government has taken several important steps to simplify business processes, promote ease of doing business, encourage entrepreneurship and create new opportunities for the youth. Khatana observed that the multimedia exhibition would serve as an effective medium for generating awareness about the welfare schemes and development initiatives of the Modi Government. Through informative displays, audio-visual presentations and other communication materials, the exhibition can help people understand the objectives, benefits and implementation of various Government programmes, he underlined. While appreciating the efforts of CBC in effectively disseminating information of GoI schemes, Khatana urged the CBC officials to organise more such exhibitions in remote areas to strengthen public outreach at the grassroot level. Expressing concern over the harmful impact of drugs, the MP called for focused awareness activities to educate people, especially youth, about the physical, psychological and social consequences of substance abuse. Earlier, Neha Jalali outlined the aims and objectives of various awareness initiatives of the Department, stating that last-mile communication remains critical to ensuring that benefits under Central Welfare Schemes reach intended beneficiaries. She briefed about various key welfare initiatives and structural reforms introduced over the past 12 years across sectors such as financial inclusion, women empowerment, healthcare, and rural infrastructure.
